title: POC Weekly Sync - Quality Eval - Elmwell Health
summary: Weekly POC sync to review quality evaluation results from the pilot, discuss prompt tuning and scoring regressions after the latest model variant test, and agree on next steps for regression harness and guardrail updates.
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-02-25 15:00 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Elmwell PM), David Kim (Elmwell ML Lead), Sara Lopez (Elmwell Security)

Summary (auto): Quick review of latest quality evals; small regression observed on clinical summaries when switching to int8 quantized variant; agreed to expand prompt sets and run 500-sample regression; Redwood to share updated scoring spreadsheet + guardrail examples; next meeting 2026-03-03.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone thanks for carving out the time. quick roll call — alex here from Redwood — priya's on the line too. Maya, David, Sara, you there?
[00:07] Maya: Yep, hi all, thanks.
[00:09] David: Here.
[00:10] Sara: present.
[00:12] Alex: Cool, agenda — go over the quality eval results Priya ran overnight, dig into the clinical summary regressions we flagged, talk prompt tuning and guardrails, and then action items.
[00:22] Priya: ok jumping in — I pushed the new eval run to the shared sheet, link in the notes — it's the sets v3 prompts against model variant Q-INT8-2026-02-20 and baseline FP16-2026-02-10.
[00:34] David: quick Q — when you say Q-INT8 was that column quantized only or did you also change the kernel selection?
[00:40] Priya: just quantization; kernel selection stayed the same. we kept the same beam/hyp sampling and temperature. those configs are in the sheet.
[00:49] Maya: high level what did you see?
[00:51] Priya: overall embedding similarity and intent classification stayed stable — within 1-2% of baseline — but clinical summary outputs show a drop in factuality scores for a subset of cases — about 6% absolute drop in our hallucination metric on the discharge summary prompt set.
[01:07] David: 6% is not insignificant. do we have examples?
[01:11] Priya: yes, I pasted 12 failing examples in the sheet. common pattern is missing negations or swapping medication dosages in ~3 cases — possibly due to tokenization differences after quant. transcription note: some proper nouns got mangled in the export.
[01:26] Alex: ok so plausible cause is quantization edge-cases on numeric tokens and rare entities — could also be prompt sensitivity. Priya, did you run with the same prompt templates?
[01:36] Priya: yes same templates. although we did notice that one template variant P3 (where we include step-by-step instructions) had better robustness.
[01:44] Maya: interesting. so maybe we tune prompts before reverting quant variant. we are sensitive to any hallucination on clinical notes — that’s a hard no for production.
[01:52] Sara: from security/compliance side — we need to capture exact model+variant in audit logs for any canary testing and ensure KMS key id is logged; also any guardrail rules we apply need to be enumerated for the audit packet.
[02:05] Alex: totally, we'll add model+variant into the tracing metadata and include that in the export.
[02:10] Priya: plan i'm proposing — step 1 expand prompt set with targeted anti-hallucination phrasing (we have 40 new prompts focusing on negation/dosage checks), step 2 run a 500-sample regression harness against both variants, step 3 automatic scoring + human spot-check for the 12 flagged examples.
[02:26] David: sounds good. timeline?
[02:28] Priya: I can run the harness tomorrow, results by Tuesday EOD — which is 2026-03-03 our next sync.
[02:35] Maya: hey can we also add a domain-specific verifier step? like post-process that checks extracted med dosages against structured fields and flags mismatches.
[02:44] Priya: yes we have a lightweight checker script — we'll wire it into the pipeline — it's not perfect but will catch simple swap errors.
[02:50] Alex: good. on guardrails — reminder we support a couple of approaches: prompt-level constraints, model-level safety filters, and post-processing rules in the Redwood console. for your use-case I'd recommend prompt + post-process to avoid false positives.
[03:03] Sara: also need the SOC2 / ISO artifacts for the pilot for procurement — we had a procurement checkpoint last week and they asked for that.
[03:11] Alex: i'll send the security pack (SOC2 summary, encryption at rest/in transit details, SSO/SAML notes) after the call.
[03:15] David: priya, can you talk briefly about scoring metrics — what are we using for factuality and how tight is the threshold?
[03:21] Priya: sure. we're combining an automatic metric — entity-level precision/recall on named clinical entities — with a model-based factuality scorer (we use entailment scoring via a BERT-style verifier) plus human rating on a 1-5 clinical correctness scale. current threshold for pass is entity F1 >= 0.88 and average human rating >= 4.2.
[03:40] Maya: and those thresholds came from our baseline discussions right? ok.
[03:44] David: how many human labels do we need for stable signal?
[03:46] Priya: we recommend 200-500 samples for initial regression detection; we proposed 500 to reduce noise and catch edge-cases.
[03:54] David: ok 500 works.
[03:56] Maya: what about latency/cost tradeoff — if we fallback to FP16 globally we incur x% cost bump — do we have numbers?
[04:05] Alex: rough math — based on your traffic profile we estimated about 18-22% cost increase per token for FP16 vs INT8 variant. latency difference minimal for your payload sizes but cost is the main driver.
[04:18] Maya: procurement will want numbers — that will factor into whether we accept small accuracy hit or not.
[04:23] Alex: we'll put a cost delta table in the shared doc.
[04:26] Priya: another note — there were a couple of transcription errors in the export — e.g., 'KMS' turned into 'KMSs' in one row; just FYI that the sheet may have small artifacts.
[04:36] David: fine. on instrumentation — if we do a canary with the quantized variant, can we route only 5% of traffic and do shadowing for another 20%?
[04:45] Alex: yes we support tiered routing and shadowing — can set up a canary policy in the console and auto-roll back if the failure rate exceeds your SLO.
[04:55] Sara: what's the failure metric we'd use to auto rollback? hallucination rate or entity F1?
[05:01] Priya: we can configure multiple triggers — primary would be entity F1 drop > 3% absolute or human-reported severe errors > 2 per 1k calls.
[05:11] Maya: will human reports be part of the automated trigger? slower but we'll still have alerts.
[05:16] Alex: human reports are a secondary signal but important; we'll wire the feedback loop into your ticketing system so triage is faster.
[05:23] David: ok good. any external competitors mentioned in the procurement thread?
[05:27] Maya: Anthropic and OpenAI popped up, mainly around hallucination comparisons. procurement is also looking at self-hosted runs with Cohere for cost reasons.
[05:35] Alex: noted. we'll include a short competitive note in the packet.
[05:39] Priya: quick demo — i pulled up three failing examples — Example A: discharge summary where dosage 5 mg got transcribed as 50 mg in quantized output. Example B: negation missing in allergy statement — 'no sulfa allergy' turned into 'sulfa allergy' in two variants. Example C: minor date swap.
[06:05] David: those are critical. do you have logs for the tokenization?
[06:08] Priya: yes — logs show different token boundaries around numerics after quantized conversion, which likely affected attention patterns. not definitive but probable.
[06:18] Maya: if we tighten prompts to emphasize exact numeric preservation, do we risk more verbosity?
[06:24] Priya: possibly; we'll test variants that ask for 'output should preserve numeric values exactly as in the input; if uncertain answer with "UNKNOWN"' which helps reduce hallucination.
[06:36] Alex: also we can add a small post-process: regex-based numeric validation and cross-check vs structured fields.
[06:42] David: good.
[06:44] Maya: on guardrails for PHI — we need data residency and encryption confirmation before we expand pilot.
[06:50] Sara: yes - confirm that logs can be redacted and that any hosted runs can be pinned to the EU region if needed.
[06:57] Alex: we can pin region and support redaction and a private deployment path if you need on-prem later. we'll include details.
[07:05] Priya: ok to recap actions: 1) Priya expands prompt set and run 500-sample regression tomorrow; 2) Alex send security pack and cost delta table; 3) Priya attach the 12 failing examples with human notes; 4) Priya and David wire the numeric verifier into the pipeline; 5) schedule next sync 2026-03-03 to review results.
[07:26] Maya: that's right.
[07:27] David: timeline fine.
[07:29] Sara: procurement will follow up via email for SOC2 doc.
[07:33] Alex: perfect. anything else?
[07:35] Maya: nope thanks.
[07:36] Alex: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the sheet and notes.

End of meeting.

Notes on transcription: occasional mislabels and punctuation; some proper nouns and acronyms may be slightly off (e.g., "KMSs" vs "KMS").
next_steps: Priya to run 500-sample regression with expanded prompts and share results by 2026-03-03
Alex to send security pack (SOC2/ISO summary, encryption details, SSO/SAML) and cost delta table by 2026-02-27
Priya to add 12 flagged examples with human annotations to the shared sheet
Priya & David to integrate numeric verifier into pipeline and report back
Schedule next sync 2026-03-03 to review regression results
